$comment: The regression gate of the small-machine budget (Wave 1 spec, §12.6). One entry
per runner class: the rate a digest of the synthetic corpus holds there and the
resident memory it may take. A run below `files_per_s` times `floor` fails, and
These are CI numbers on a shared runner, not the budget: the budget is measured
on the baseline host of C6 and lives in the design record. What this file gates
is drift — a change that halves the rate must be a change someone meant to make,
and updating these numbers is a commit of its own that says why.
The `stages` numbers are Wave 2's: a fingerprint and a classification of the same corpus, in stacks a second rather than files.

The `stages` gate numbers are set well under what the runner measures, for the same reason the digest one is and more so: a fingerprint or a classification of this corpus takes about a tenth of a second, and a tenth of a second on a shared runner is mostly noise. The same commit measured 13,861 stacks/s one day and 11,044 the next with the classifier unchanged. These numbers are here to fail on a halving, which they still do.

Linux-X64.note: the gate number is set below what the runner measured on purpose: a shared runner varies by a quarter run to run, and this is here to catch a real regression, not to measure the machine

measured.note: 4,144 stacks/s on the runner; 4,437 the day before
11,044 stacks/s on the runner; 13,861 the day before; 13,300 on a quiet machine
